questions.q: Why is the iron and steel industry called a basic industry, and where is it located in India?

answer.text: The iron and steel industry is called a basic, or key, industry because its products, iron and steel, are the raw materials for many other industries. Machinery, tools, vehicles, railways, ships and construction all depend on steel. The growth of this industry therefore drives the growth of the entire manufacturing sector, which is why it is regarded as the backbone of industrial development.

The industry needs bulky raw materials, iron ore, coal and limestone, so plants are located close to their sources to reduce transport costs. In India most steel plants are concentrated on and around the Chotanagpur plateau in the east, which is rich in these materials. The first modern plant was set up by TISCO at Jamshedpur, followed by public sector plants at Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur and Bokaro.

answer: Thus its central role and its location near raw materials make iron and steel a basic industry.

questions.q: How do means of transport act as the lifelines of India's economy?

answer.text: are the lifelines of India's economy because they move people and goods and tie the country together.

list: They carry raw materials to factories and finished goods to markets, keeping trade and industry going
They move people for work, education and tourism across the country
Roads, railways, waterways and airways link remote areas to the mainstream, promoting national integration
The dense railway network and the growing road system are especially vital to India's vast and varied land

questions.q: How has modern communication transformed life and the economy in India?

answer.text: has rapidly transformed life and the economy in India by linking people and spreading information swiftly.

list: Telephones, mobile phones and the internet connect people across the country and the world instantly
Mass media — television, radio and newspapers — spread news, education and awareness

list: The spread of mobile phones and the internet has enabled the growth of IT, e-commerce and online services
